questions.question: Earth orbits the Sun with period $T_E = 1\ \mathrm{yr}$ at radius $r_E = 1\ \mathrm{AU}$. Mars has orbital radius $r_M = 1.52\ \mathrm{AU}$. Using Kepler's Third Law, find the orbital period of Mars in years.
questions.answer:
Kepler's Third Law: $T^2 \propto r^3$, so $\dfrac{T_M^2}{T_E^2} = \dfrac{r_M^3}{r_E^3}$

$T_M = T_E \left(\dfrac{r_M}{r_E}\right)^{3/2} = 1 \times (1.52)^{3/2}$

$(1.52)^{3/2} = 1.52 \times \sqrt{1.52} = 1.52 \times 1.233 = 1.874$

$$T_M \approx 1.87\ \mathrm{yr}$$

questions.question: A satellite has orbital period $T = 24\ \mathrm{h}$ (geostationary). Earth's surface gravity is $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ and radius $R = 6400\ \mathrm{km}$. Find the orbital radius of this geostationary satellite.
Derive the orbital period formula $T = 2\pi\sqrt{r^3/(GM)}$ for a circular orbit of radius $r$ around a body of mass $M$.
questions.answer:
For circular orbit, gravitational force provides centripetal acceleration:

$\dfrac{GMm}{r^2} = \dfrac{mv^2}{r} \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$

The circumference is $2\pi r$, so the period is:

$T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{v} = \dfrac{2\pi r}{\sqrt{GM/r}} = 2\pi r \cdot \sqrt{\dfrac{r}{GM}}$

$$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{GM}}$$

Squaring: $T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{GM}r^3$, confirming $T^2 \propto r^3$ (Kepler's Third Law).

questions.question: A moon orbits a planet of mass $M$ at radius $r_1$ with period $T_1$. A second moon orbits the same planet at radius $r_2 = 4r_1$. Find the period $T_2$ of the second moon.
questions.answer:
By Kepler's Third Law:

$\dfrac{T_2^2}{T_1^2} = \dfrac{r_2^3}{r_1^3} = \left(\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}\right)^3 = 4^3 = 64$

$T_2 = T_1 \sqrt{64} = 8T_1$

The second moon (4 times farther out) has a period 8 times longer.

questions.question: A satellite orbits Earth at height $h = 400\ \mathrm{km}$ above the surface. Find its orbital speed. Use $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, $R_E = 6400\ \mathrm{km}$.
questions.answer:
Orbital radius: $r = R_E + h = 6400 + 400 = 6800\ \mathrm{km} = 6.8\times10^6\ \mathrm{m}$

Using $GM = gR_E^2$:

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{gR_E^2}{r}} = R_E\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{r}}$

$= 6.4\times10^6 \times \sqrt{\dfrac{9.8}{6.8\times10^6}}$

$= 6.4\times10^6 \times \sqrt{1.441\times10^{-6}}$

$= 6.4\times10^6 \times 1.2\times10^{-3} \approx 7680\ \mathrm{m/s} \approx 7.68\ \mathrm{km/s}$

questions.question: Three planets A, B, C orbit the same star. Their orbital radii are in the ratio $r_A : r_B : r_C = 1 : 4 : 9$. Find the ratio of their orbital periods.

Use Kepler's Third Law and the Earth–Moon system to estimate the Moon's orbital radius. The Moon's orbital period is $T = 27.3\ \mathrm{days}$. Use $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$, $R_E = 6.4\times10^6\ \mathrm{m}$.

A planet orbits a star of mass $M_s = 2\times10^{30}\ \mathrm{kg}$ with period $T = 1\ \mathrm{yr} = 3.15\times10^7\ \mathrm{s}$. Find the orbital radius. Use $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}\ \mathrm{N\cdot m^2/kg^2}$.
questions.answer:
$r^3 = \dfrac{GM_s T^2}{4\pi^2}$

$= \dfrac{6.67\times10^{-11} \times 2\times10^{30} \times (3.15\times10^7)^2}{4\pi^2}$

$= \dfrac{6.67\times10^{-11} \times 2\times10^{30} \times 9.92\times10^{14}}{39.48}$

$= \dfrac{1.323\times10^{35}}{39.48} \approx 3.35\times10^{33}\ \mathrm{m^3}$

$r = (3.35\times10^{33})^{1/3} \approx 1.50\times10^{11}\ \mathrm{m} = 1.50\times10^8\ \mathrm{km}$

This is 1 AU — Earth's actual orbital radius ✓

questions.question: A satellite in a circular orbit at radius $r$ from Earth's center has speed $v_1$. Another satellite orbits at radius $3r$. Find its speed $v_2$ in terms of $v_1$.
questions.answer:
For circular orbit: $v = \sqrt{GM/r}$, so $v \propto r^{-1/2}$

$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{r}{3r}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$$v_2 = \dfrac{v_1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}v_1 \approx 0.577\,v_1$$

**Period comparison:** $T \propto r^{3/2}$, so $T_2 = T_1(3)^{3/2} = 3\sqrt{3}\,T_1$

questions.question: Earth's orbital period around the Sun is $T_E = 1\ \mathrm{yr}$ and orbital radius is $r_E = 1\ \mathrm{AU}$. An asteroid has orbital radius $r_A = 4\ \mathrm{AU}$. (a) Find its period. (b) If the asteroid starts at the same position as Earth at $t = 0$, how long before they are at the same angular position again (first synodic period)?
questions.answer:
**(a)** $T_A = T_E (r_A/r_E)^{3/2} = 1 \times 4^{3/2} = 8\ \mathrm{yr}$

**(b)** The synodic period $S$ satisfies:

$\dfrac{1}{S} = \dfrac{1}{T_E} - \dfrac{1}{T_A} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{7}{8}$

$S = \dfrac{8}{7} \approx 1.14\ \mathrm{yr}$

(Earth laps the slower asteroid every 8/7 years.)
